# PR #5101: Patch: daily super run failed

Closes #5085

Closes #5085.

Super run 45831405859 tested `_staging` at `2682cb7`. That commit does not include three pull requests, now on `main`, that fix seven of its eight red jobs. One test in the eighth job was still flaky on `main`; this pull request makes it fast instead of raising its timeout. I re-ran every failed job's own command on the base, `4dabf5c94f`, and each passes there.

## What changed

The test that could time out was `apps/web/src/fx/layerBudget.test.ts`'s `R4493000 no element of any DOM cue covers more than FX_LAYER_MAX_SCREENS`. It estimated every DOM cue in one test, under vitest's default 5000 ms timeout. The planner measured it at 3595 ms inside the full job on an idle 4-core machine, and at 6475 ms, a failure, on a slower one. Three causes, fixed in two test-only files:

- **The keyframes were re-read for every cue.** `apps/web/src/test/layerEstimate.ts` scanned the keyframe bodies of `fx.css` (330 KB) on every `estimateLayers` call. They are now read once per sheet, kept with the rule index that `indexOf` already caches. The new field is typed `ReadonlyMap`, so typecheck fails if anything writes to the shared map.
- **The design tokens were re-installed for every cue.** `layersOf` called `installTokens()` each time, re-parsing three stylesheets and setting about 100 properties per cue. It now runs once, in the describe's `beforeAll`. Nothing under `src/fx/` writes the document element's style, and the doc comment records that assumption.
- **One test did all the work.** It is now `it.each` over `CASES`' 30 cue kinds: `R4493000 no element of any %s cue covers more than FX_LAYER_MAX_SCREENS`. Together the 30 tests assert exactly what the one did.

There is no new ruling, spec change, patches fragment, timeout or config change.
